newsitem.title: FRANCE: Embattled Mobutu leaves France for Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Embattled Mobutu leaves France for Zaire.

text.p: Zaire's ailing President Mobutu Sese Seko left France for home on Friday in a last-ditch attempt to save his crumbling authority in the face of growing support for rebels led by Laurent Kabila.

The 66-year-old Zairean leader, who has spent most of his time in Europe since he had prostate cancer surgery last August, took off from Nice airport to Kinshasa after calling on Thursday for national unity and for a ceasefire rejected by the rebels.

Mobutu, who left hospital in Monaco on Wednesday after fresh cancer treatment and had not been seen in public for weeks, was driven to the airport in a six-car convoy escorted by French police and boarded a white DC8 after waving to aides.

His son and spokesman Mobutu Nzanga told Reuters his father would meet Prime Minister Kengo wa Dondo and armed forces chief of staff General General Mahele Lieko Bokoungo as soon as he arrived in Kinshasa and would broadcast to the nation.
"He will address the nation to mark his position clearly," Nzanga said. "My father remains an important player in the stability of central Africa."
In a statement issued on Thursday night, Mobutu called on Zaireans "to rise together" and proposed creating a national council to solve the country's crisis.
But in Kisangani, the third-largest Zairean town which they captured last Saturday, the rebels rejected his call for a truce and said he was only trying to buy time.
"We do not receive Mobutu's orders. If Mobutu comes back, it makes no difference," rebel political commissioner Deo Bugera said.
France and the United States have made contingency plans to evacuate their nationals from Zaire if necessary. France has positioned its troops and planes in nearby Gabon and Congo.
Mobutu, in power for 32 years, has been threatened by armed opponents before, but rebels have never made such deep advances and his ill-disciplined army has rarely performed as poorly.
But Nzanga said: "A good part of the army remains loyal. It has been highly motivated by the appointment last autumn of General Mahele."
Nzanga decribed the events in eastern Zaire, where the rebels have captured more than a fifth of the country, as "ethnic cleansing due to the hatred between Tutsis and Hutus".
He said his father's first priority would be to settle a standoff over an attempt by the transitional parliament earlier this week to sack the prime minister.

Nzanga once again denied reports his father was seriously ill, revived by Mobutu's last-minute cancellation of a planned photo opportunity on his French Riviera villa on Thursday and by the way photographers were kept outside the airport perimeter on his departure.
Photographs taken through the window of his fast-moving car showed the president looking solemn in a business suit and his trademark leopard-skin hat.
"The president is well. He received six visitors yesterday, including two Europeans," Nzanga said.
Aides said Mobutu was deeply angered by a report issued by the Congolese Red Cross that members of his family had fled Zaire to neighbouring Congo.
"I deny that any of my close family has left Kinshasa. The president's own sister is still in Kinshasa," Nzanga said.
